content.title: About
content.content: Whiting (a member of the cod family) is a lean white‑fleshed fish that is commonly baked or broiled. It has a mild flavor, low fat content, and a high protein level, making it a popular choice for healthy meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whiting is found in the cold waters of the North Atlantic and the Baltic Sea.
In the United States, whiting is often sold as fillets and used in fish‑and‑chips style dishes.
The fish can grow up to 30 cm in length and weigh around 300 g.
A 100 g serving provides roughly 85 kcal, making it a low‑calorie protein source.
Whiting is traditionally used in European coastal cuisines, especially in fried preparations.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A 100 g portion supplies about 18 g of complete protein, essential for muscle maintenance and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Whiting contains very little saturated fat, suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It provides vitamin B12, niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals: selenium and iodine
items.content: Whiting is a good source of selenium, an antioxidant, and iodine, important for thyroid health.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Although lower than in fatty fish, whiting still contributes omega‑3s that help cardiovascular health.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, including whiting.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: As a marine species, whiting can contain trace amounts of mercury and other heavy metals; moderate consumption is advised.

items.title: Nutrient loss with overcooking
items.content: Excessive baking or broiling can degrade heat‑sensitive vitamins such as B12.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Season whiting fillets with herbs, lemon, and a drizzle of olive oil, then bake or broil until opaque and flaky. Serve with steamed vegetables, roasted potatoes, or whole‑grain salads. The mild flesh also works well in fish tacos, soups, or as a protein addition to grain bowls.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh whiting refrigerated at 0‑2 °C, wrapped in plastic or placed in an airtight container, and use within 2 days. Frozen fillets store at –18 °C for up to 6 months. Discard any fish with a strong, ammonia‑like odor, as it indicates spoilage.
